description:
pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:138 doc says: 'cycle detection uses subject-DN equality to avoid quadratic memory.'

Actual implementation (lines 143-174) uses NO DN-equality cycle detection. It uses a step counter (`max_steps = bundle.len() + 1`) and returns false when exceeded. A walk through an A→B→A cycle would take N+1 steps and then bail — correct (fail-closed) but not via DN equality.

The 'avoid quadratic memory' phrase suggests the alternative considered was a visited-set, which would be O(N) memory not O(N²). The doc is wrong on two counts: no DN-equality check exists, and the rejected alternative would be O(N) memory not quadratic.

Fix: rewrite the doc comment to describe the actual mechanism — 'A bounded step counter caps the walk at bundle.len() + 1 iterations; longer chains (or cycles) fail closed by returning false.' Drop the inaccurate cycle-detection-via-DN-equality claim.
title: reaches_self_signed doc claims DN-equality cycle detection; code uses step-bound
